title: Hackers Exploit Metabase Flaw in Mathspace Data Breach Affecting 1.07 Million Users
content_md: Mathspace, a mathematics learning platform used by schools in Australia and New Zealand, has disclosed a data breach affecting 1,079,819 students, parents or guardians, teachers, and employees. The incident stemmed from the exploitation of a critical vulnerability in a self-hosted Metabase reporting deployment, which gave an attacker administrator-level access without legitimate credentials. Mathspace said it confirmed the intrusion on September 3 after reviewing access logs. The company determined that unauthorized access began on August 10, Australian Eastern Standard Time, and that data was exported from its Australian reporting database on August 27. Hackers Exploit Metabase Flaw The breach followed Metabase’s publication of a critical security advisory and the release of patched versions on August 6. Mathspace acknowledged that its vulnerability-notification process did not identify and escalate the advisory. It updated the Metabase instance on August 29 after learning of a subsequent notice, but did not complete compromise checks recommended for potentially affected environments. Subsequent log analysis established that the attacker had accessed the system before the patch was applied. The exposed export contained user IDs, usernames, first and last names, email addresses, country and time zone data, user types, email verification status, and account metadata, including last active, last login, and account creation dates.
